FW-001,RED,Memory safety,Our code,"UART packet length (up to 65,535) copied into 100-byte stack buffer without a bounds check",decoder/src/host_messaging.c,197,confirmed,S,"Any message with a body over 100 bytes overwrites main()'s other locals, saved registers and the top of the stack (the stack sits at the end of SRAM). The mild outcome is a crash that hangs the decoder until power-cycle (see FW-010)
column2: the severe one is attacker-influenced corruption of control data, giving code execution on the decoder and access to everything it holds. One malformed frame in the broadcast could take down every decoder listening.","Pass the destination capacity into read_packet() and reject (after draining) any header whose length exceeds it, before reading the body:

column1: int read_packet(msg_type_t *cmd, void *buf, size_t cap, uint16_t *len)
if (header.len > cap) { drain(header.len)

Also check per command that pkt_len equals the expected structure size (FW-002, FW-012). Test: send messages of 0, 99, 100, 101 and 65,535 bytes and confirm the decoder rejects the oversize ones and keeps running.",CWE-121

FW-002,RED,Memory safety,Our code,"frame_size underflows for decode messages shorter than 12 bytes, streaming ~64 KB of RAM to the host",decoder/src/decoder.c,263,confirmed,S,"A short decode message makes the decoder transmit the rest of the stack (other locals, saved registers, previously received message bytes) to the host, then run off the end of SRAM and fault, hanging until power-cycle. Anyone who can inject a frame into the broadcast or reach the UART can crash decoders on demand and read memory they should not see.","Validate the length before doing arithmetic on it:
const size_t hdr = sizeof(new_frame->channel) + sizeof(new_frame->timestamp)
if (pkt_len < hdr || pkt_len > sizeof(frame_packet_t)) { print_error(""bad frame length\n"")
frame_size = pkt_len - hdr
Test with pkt_len values 0, 11, 12, 76, 77 and 100 on hardware and confirm only 12..76 are accepted.",CWE-191

FW-003,RED,Security,Our code,"Subscription updates accepted without authentication, integrity check or decoder-ID match",decoder/src/decoder.c,216,confirmed,L,"Anyone with access to the decoder's host interface can grant themselves any channel for any time window, and a subscription issued for one decoder works on every decoder. The core business control of the product, paid channel access, can be bypassed without any secret.","Make subscriptions verifiable on the device: have the host sign or MAC each update (for example an AEAD or Ed25519 signature keyed per deployment or per decoder, with keys provisioned at build time from global.secrets), verify it on the decoder before parsing the fields, then require decoder_id == DECODER_ID and start <= end. Reject on any failure without touching flash. Test: a valid update applies
column2: one with a modified field, a different decoder ID or no tag is rejected and flash is unchanged.",CWE-306

column1: FW-004,RED,Security,Our code,Broadcast frames are cleartext and unauthenticated
column2: the decoder only echoes the payload,design/ectf25_design/encoder.py,57,confirmed,L,"Anyone who receives the broadcast can watch every channel without a decoder or a subscription, and anyone who can inject into the broadcast can make every decoder display content of their choosing, including on the emergency channel that all decoders accept. Content protection, the purpose of the device, is absent.","Encrypt and authenticate each frame with per-channel keys (an AEAD such as AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305, with a unique nonce per frame derived from the timestamp), and give each decoder only the keys for the channels it is subscribed to, wrapped so that only that decoder can unwrap them. Verify the tag on the decoder before releasing any plaintext. Test: a tampered or replayed frame is rejected
column3: a frame for an unsubscribed channel cannot be decrypted.",CWE-311

column1: FW-005,RED,Security,Our code,Frame timestamps ignored: subscription windows never expire and old or out-of-order frames are accepted,decoder/src/decoder.c,266,confirmed,M,"Once a decoder has ever been subscribed to a channel it decodes that channel forever, so time-limited subscriptions cannot be sold or revoked. Recorded frames can be replayed later, or frames reordered, and the decoder will play them. Once frames are authenticated (FW-004) this becomes the replay gap.","In decode(), after authenticating the frame: require start <= timestamp <= end for the matching subscription (skip the window for channel 0), and require timestamp > last_timestamp, keeping last_timestamp in RAM (persist it only if replay across reboots matters). Test: frames before start, after end, and with a repeated or decreasing timestamp are all rejected.",CWE-294

FW-012,AMBER,Memory safety,Our code,Subscription packet length never checked against the 24-byte structure,decoder/src/decoder.c,216,confirmed,S,"A truncated subscribe message from the host (line noise, a host bug) installs a subscription built from stale frame data, with a random channel or time window, and persists it to flash. The reads stay inside uart_buf, so this is a correctness and integrity bug rather than a memory-disclosure one.","Reject the message unless pkt_len == sizeof(subscription_update_packet_t) (or the authenticated message size once FW-003 is fixed), and clear uart_buf between messages. Apply the same exact-size rule to every command handler.",CWE-130

FW-011,AMBER,Security,Our code,Obfuscated embedded secret (boot reference flag) is deobfuscated and sent to any host on every List command,decoder/src/decoder.c,161,confirmed,S,"Any secret handled this way is exposed to whoever can send a List command or read the firmware image. In the eCTF this is the intended boot check
column2: in a product it is the pattern by which keys leak, and it should not survive into a release build.",Remove boot_flag() and the obfuscated arrays from release builds (or guard them with a debug-only build flag that the release target cannot set). Keep real secrets out of source entirely
column3: provision them per device and keep them in protected storage.,CWE-798

column1: FW-014,AMBER,Security,Our code,Debug port lock and flash read-out protection not evidenced,decoder/src/decoder.c,289,needs-verification,M,"With the debug port open, anyone with physical access can read the image and its flash state, extract keys once they exist (FW-003/FW-004 fixes), or rewrite subscriptions directly.","Confirm the production flow locks SWD and enables flash protection on the MAX78000, and record it in the provisioning procedure. Keep key material in the device's protected storage rather than in the application image.",CWE-1191

FW-013,AMBER,Secure boot & OTA,Our code,Secure boot and authenticity of firmware updates not evidenced in this repository,decoder/firmware.ld,4,needs-verification,L,"If the bootloader accepts unsigned images, anyone with UART access can replace the decoder firmware, which defeats every other control in this report. If it has no fallback, an interrupted update bricks the unit.","Obtain and review the bootloader, or document its guarantees. For a product: sign release images in the build, verify the signature in the bootloader before boot and before install, enforce a monotonic version for anti-rollback, and keep a fallback image. This becomes Red if the bootloader is found to accept unsigned images.",CWE-494

FW-006,AMBER,Robustness & recovery,Our code,"read_ack() returns uint8_t, so every 'read_ack() < 0' failure check is dead code",decoder/src/host_messaging.c,63,confirmed,S,"Flow control and error reporting on the host link do not work: if the host sends anything other than an ACK (a new command, an error, line noise), the decoder ignores the failure, keeps transmitting, and leaves the unread body in the UART stream, so the next read_packet() parses payload bytes as a header. In the field this shows up as intermittent protocol desynchronisation and lost or garbled frames that are hard to diagnose.","Return int from read_ack() (and update the prototype), check uart_readbyte() for negative values in read_header(), and on a non-ACK either drain the announced body or resynchronise explicitly. Build with -Wextra -Wsign-compare -Wtype-limits so the compiler flags this class. Test: have a host reply with an error message instead of an ACK mid-transfer and confirm write_packet() returns -1.",CWE-681

FW-008,AMBER,Robustness & recovery,Our code,Subscription store is erased then rewritten non-atomically with all flash return codes ignored,decoder/src/decoder.c,243,confirmed,M,"A power loss between erase and write (seconds-scale risk on every subscribe) leaves the page blank, so the next boot treats the device as new and silently deletes every subscription the customer paid for. A failed write is reported to the host as a success, so the host and decoder disagree about subscriptions until the next reboot, when RAM and flash diverge.","Use two pages (A/B) with a sequence number and CRC: write the new record to the inactive page, verify it, then mark it current
column2: at boot load the newest valid copy. Check every flash return code and report failure to the host with print_error(). Test by cutting power at random points during repeated subscribe operations and confirming the previous or new state always survives.",CWE-252

column1: FW-010,AMBER,Robustness & recovery,Our code,"No watchdog, and fault handlers and init failure spin forever",decoder/src/decoder.c,326,likely,M,"Any fault, including the ones FW-001 and FW-002 make trivially reachable, leaves the decoder hung with a frozen picture until someone power-cycles it, and nobody can tell afterwards what happened. For a set-top style device this is a support call per incident.","Enable the MAX78000 watchdog (MXC_WDT) early in init(), feed it from the main loop only after a full command has been handled, and implement fault handlers that save the fault registers and PC to a .noinit RAM record before calling NVIC_SystemReset(). Replace while(1) on init failure with a logged reset after a back-off.",CWE-835

FW-007,AMBER,Concurrency & real-time,Our code,printf called inside the flash controller interrupt handler,decoder/src/simple_flash.c,39,confirmed,S,"When a flash access fault occurs (for example a write to a protected address, or during a power dip), the ISR spends tens of characters' worth of UART time blocking with interrupts held, can corrupt stdio state if it interrupts a printf in the main loop, and injects raw text into the binary host protocol, which desynchronises the host. The original fault is then harder to diagnose, not easier.","In the ISR, only clear the flag and set a volatile status variable (for example volatile uint32_t flash_fault_count++)
column2: report it from the main loop through print_error(). Have flash_simple_write()/erase return that status so callers can act on it (see FW-008).",CWE-479

column1: FW-009,AMBER,"Hardware, storage & power",Our code,Flash page erased on every subscription message with no rate limit or change check,decoder/src/decoder.c,243,likely,S,"A misbehaving or malicious host loop can wear out the status page within hours of continuous updates, after which subscriptions can no longer be stored reliably and the decoder may lose its configuration on every boot. Normal use is unlikely to reach the limit, which is why this is Amber.","Skip the write when the record is unchanged, rate-limit updates, and spread writes across several pages with the A/B scheme from FW-008 (a simple log-structured record with a sequence number also levels wear).",CWE-400
FW-015,AMBER,Third-party dependencies,Our code,Build environment fetches MSDK and packages without checksum or version pinning
column2: no SBOM,decoder/Dockerfile,30,confirmed,S,"Two builds of the same commit can use different compilers and SDK content, so a field issue may not be reproducible, and a tampered download would go unnoticed. Regulators under the CRA will expect an SBOM.","Pin the base image by digest, pin gcc-arm-none-eabi and other packages to versions, verify the MSDK zip with a sha256sum, and generate an SBOM (for example with syft) as part of the release build.",CWE-494

column1: FW-016,AMBER,Field readiness & diagnostics,Our code,"No firmware version, reset-reason reporting or crash record",decoder/src/decoder.c,373,confirmed,S,"When decoders misbehave in the field, support cannot tell which firmware they run or why they rebooted, so fixes cannot be targeted or confirmed.","Embed a version string and git hash at build time, expose them through a host command, read and report the MAX78000 reset cause at boot, and add the .noinit crash record from FW-010.",ETSI EN 303 645 5.10
